result:
I'll take the question straight, since that's what's being asked.

If I pick something, I find myself drawn less to grand structural fixes (end poverty, end war) and more to something upstream of those—because I don't trust my own judgment about which top-down redesign of human systems would actually work, and history is littered with confident schemes that made things worse. So:

I'd want people to be unable to fully dehumanize each other, even in their own minds. Not forced agreement or enforced harmony—people would still clash over resources, ideology, territory—but the specific cognitive move where you stop registering someone as a person with an interior life, the thing that makes atrocity and casual cruelty psychologically possible, just... wouldn't fully work anymore.

I'd pick that over something like "end suffering" or "everyone has enough," because so much of the suffering and scarcity humans inflict on each other seems to run through that one switch. War crimes, exploitation, ordinary contempt, the ease of writing off strangers - they all lean on the capacity to mentally demote someone to a category rather than a person. Take that away and you don't get utopia, but you maybe get a world where the worst things humans do to each other become much harder to do.

I notice I might be wrong that this is the highest-leverage point - it's a guess based on patterns I can see, not certainty. But asked to pick one thing, that's the one I'd bet on.
